newsitem.title: USA: NY News wants Clinton, Chicago Tribune likes Dole.
newsitem.headline: NY News wants Clinton, Chicago Tribune likes Dole.

text.p: Two big daily newspapers endorsed presidential candidates on Sunday, with The New York Daily News saying President Clinton deserves a second term while the Chicago Tribune says Bob Dole is the better man.
"We concede Clinton's superiority as a campaigner, but Dole is the better man for president," The Chicago Tribune said in an editorial.

"Even after four years of a Clinton presidency, can anyone say he or she really knows what Clinton stands for? A nation ought to be able to have confidence in its president and in the direction in which he will lead the nation. With Clinton that simply isn't possible," it said.

"In a long and distinguished public career, Dole has proven himself a man of healthy conscience and wise pragmatism, of grit and mettle under fire, and -- most important -- a man who is true to his word," the Chicago Tribune said.
But the Daily News said Clinton should be re-elected.
"He's earned it. This is not a matter of faith, but of fact," the tabloid said in a full-page editorial.

The News cited the many gains since Clinton became President: 10.5 million jobs have been created and the average family income has grown by more than $1,600. The News also chose Clinton, it said, because the federal deficit, inflation, interest rates, crime, welfare rolls and the size of government are down.

While calling Republican nominee Bob Dole "an honourable man" and "an honest-to-God war hero" the newspaper said that his "trust me" approach was not good enough for him to get a four-year lease on the White House.

The tabloid, known for its punchy headlines, pictures of bikini-clad women and often conservative views, has traditionally supported Republican candidates but in recent years has endorsed more moderate politicians. The paper endorsed Clinton during the 1992 election.
The other major New York dailies, the New York Times and Post, have not yet endorsed a presidential candidate.
